record.question: Which minimal records separate equivalent production graphs?
record.what_happened: Discrimination by record level: artifact 50%, timings 50%, proposals 50%, alternatives 50%, accept_veto 50%, role_map 47%, full_log 100%; the first level reaching 75% was full_log.
record.what_changed_in_the_project_world: The information-value ladder names the minimal record a text-side reader would need before any director claim.

hypothesis: Adding records one level at a time, from timings to the full log, maps which records separate a director from an equivalent shared brief; the minimal sufficient set is the first level that does.

gates.name: live:records_add_discrimination
gates.detail: the intervention changes the intended latent or policy

gates.name: placebo:artifact_alone_at_chance
gates.detail: an irrelevant matched intervention does not change the target

gates.name: positive:full_log_separates
gates.detail: a known readable manipulation is recovered

gates.name: surface:no_artifact_shortcut
gates.detail: cheap source, length, count, label or entropy cues cannot solve the card

gates.name: oracle:identifiable_with_records
gates.detail: the target is identifiable when the correct variables are supplied

gates.name: prediction:role_map_gain
gates.detail: the inferred object constrains a held-out choice, continuation, probe or response

gates.name: calibration:timings_less_than_roles
gates.detail: the reference is floored at chance: where the role map itself separates nothing, a below-chance classifier wobble is not a standard the timing level can be held to

gates_summary.how_to_read: a gate RECORDS here and does not raise, so an exploratory sweep is never killed mid-run. tests/test_gates.py walks every committed verdict and fails the suite on anything in failed_names or unexpected_passes, which puts the hard stop where a result would become public. THREE categories, and they are not the same thing: failed_names is a control that broke; documented_failures is a gate marked expected_to_fail, which records a KNOWN defect so the evidence travels with the result (S-2's dead manipulation, S-3's fitted threshold); unexpected_passes is a documented defect that has started passing, which means somebody fixed it without updating the gate and is the one nobody would otherwise notice. A skipped gate counts as passing but is reported separately: it means an optional dependency was absent, never that a check succeeded.
